title: Failure catalog and actionable observability canvas for inference errors
creator: Aisha Martinez
body: Goal: Build a concise, operationally-actionable failure catalog for inference traffic and deliver a focused dashboard + runbook integration that helps oncall and SREs identify root cause classes (timeouts, overload, model errors, transport codes) within 3 minutes. This ticket covers: 1) defining a failure vocabulary with stable semantic tags, 2) tracehook enrichment and metric/log label changes, 3) a single-pane dashboard (Actionable Observability Canvas) with pivoting by failure class, kernel/hardware type, model variant, and route, and 4) linking each failure bucket to a first-response play and automated triage hints.
problem_statement: Current error dashboards flood oncall with noisy alerts and inconclusive traces. Root cause requires manual correlation across traces, model logs, and GPU/job metrics. We lack a canonical mapping from RPC/HTTP/gRPC status codes and model runtime signals to operator-level failure classes, making paging decisions and automated remediation brittle.
success_metrics: reduction in false-positive incident pages by 30%
percentage of incidents auto-tagged by tracehooks >= 70%
playbook engaged within 5m for high-impact errors
failure_vocabulary: timeout.client_wall: request exceeded client deadline (wall clock)
timeout.kv_prefetch: KV cache prefetch latency exceeded threshold during prefix fetch
overload.enqueue: request queued beyond target latency (backpressure)
overload.gpu_saturation: GPU util or queue length causing token latency spikes
model.invalid_response: model produced malformed/empty/unsafe output or function-call mismatch
model.oom: model or runtime OOM during generation/compile
transport.4xx: upstream/proxy client errors (4xx) mapped to request validation
transport.5xx: upstream/service errors (5xx) mapped to infra or model crash
routing.mismatch: request routed to incompatible model variant triggering decoding errors
data_model_changes: tracehook: add field failure_class (enum) and failure_tags (list) to root span
metrics: expose failure_class label on request_count, failure_rate, p50/p95 latency metrics
logs: enrich structured logs with failure_class and kernel_hint (e.g., 'ggml_q4_0', 'cuda_ampere_fused')
sampling: increase span sampling to 50% for requests tagged as high-cost (long sequence) for first 72h post-rollout
dashboard_requirements: Canvas view with primary pivot = failure_class, secondary = model_variant, tertiary = region/hardware
Top-N failure contributors with heatmap of failure_rate x Q95 latency
Quick filters: time-window, route, release tag, kernel_hint
Trace-link panel that surfaces earliest failure span and suggested playbook action
Drilldown to raw logs and recent deploys for correlated release tags
acceptance_criteria: Canonical failure taxonomy documented in Confluence and linked from dashboard
Tracehooks populate failure_class for >= 70% of erroring requests in the canary tenant
Dashboard shows failure breakdown and links to runbook entries for each class
Oncall-runbook automated hints appear in Slack incident channel when a P0 failure_class fires
technical_approach: Phase 1: Draft taxonomy and mapping rules (this ticket) with input from runtime, infra, and model teams
Phase 2: Implement tracehook enrichment in request gateway runtime and instrument kernel/hardware hints
Phase 3: Update metric/OLAP ingestion pipeline to accept failure_class labels and backfill 7d of data for baseline
Phase 4: Build Grafana/Lens canvas with JSON model, wire trace links and runbook actions
Phase 5: Canary with internal tenants -> roll to prod
rollout_plan: Week 1 (canary): Enable tracehook enrichment for internal-canary services, sampling=100% for errors
Week 2: Observe, tune taxonomy rules; reduce noisy buckets; backfill dashboards
Week 3: Enable enrichment for 25% of prod tenants; enable alerts with muted thresholds
Week 4: Full prod rollout and schedule postmortem review
runbook_integration: Map each failure_class to a primary action: Retry(with-jitter), Increase-burst-capacity, Re-route-to-fallback-model, Investigate-model-stage, Escalate-to-Model-NRE
Attach checklist links for diagnostics: kernel logs, GPU metrics, kv-cache miss rate, recent deploys
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-tagging leads to noisy classification -> Mitigation: conservative initial taxonomy + human review queue
Risk: Increased trace volume costs -> Mitigation: sampling window and adaptive rate lowering after stable threshold
Risk: Mapping breaks for new model families -> Mitigation: taxonomy extensions gated by model-onboarding checklist
tasks: Draft taxonomy rules and publish Confluence doc
Implement tracehook change in gateway (PR: github.com/redwoodinc/gateway/pull/4291)
Add failure_class label in metrics exporter and update ingestion schema
Create Grafana canvas and dashboard JSON
Author per-class runbook entries and Slack automation
Run canary, collect metrics, and iterate
updates: 2025-02-11: Kickoff meeting with runtime and obs teams. Agreed on initial 9 failure classes.
2025-02-15: Design review -- Priya provided layout feedback to emphasize 'time-to-classify' and trace-link prominence.
2025-02-18: Gateway tracehook prototype implemented (branch) and unit tests added. PR opened.
2025-02-21: Observability ingestion change reviewed; schema bump approved for console-2025.03 release.

2025-02-24: Internal canary for the 'model.oom' and 'timeout.client_wall' classes enabled. Early results: auto-classification rate 68% for erroring requests and 12% reduction in false-positive pages during test window.
2025-02-27: PM feedback: add kernel_hint and route labels to dashboard pivots; adjusted acceptance criteria to 70% auto-tagging before wide rollout.
next_steps: Merge gateway PR and coordinate deploy window with infra maintenance (ETA 2025-03-03)
Complete dashboard JSON and link runbook actions into Slack incident workflow
Schedule 72h canary monitoring and post-canary retro
